context.scope: Action started by a person in the ExportReg screen of Editing policy files directly: Writes the chosen branch of the policy file to a .reg file
rules: Export to a registry script is refused until a file name is given; the person is told "Please specify a filename and path for the exported REG." (PolicyPlus/ExportReg.vb:20)

When the registry script is written, the person is told "REG exported successfully." and the dialog closes; on any failure they are told only "Failed to export REG!" and the dialog stays open. (PolicyPlus/ExportReg.vb:27)

When a value is marked for deletion in a policy file, any value or marker already held under that name is dropped first. A deletion marker holding the number 32, as Microsoft does, is added unless the value is already marked or its key is cleared. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:92)
When a value is forgotten in a policy file, both the value and its deletion marker are removed, so the policy reverts to not saying anything about it. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:99)
When a value is set in a policy file, it replaces any value already held under that name. A deletion marker for the name is not removed. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:105)

When a REG file is written, a default value is shown as an at sign, and quotes and backslashes in names and text are escaped. Text is written as quoted text and a 32-bit number as 'dword:' with eight hexadecimal digits. Every other type, including 64-bit numbers, expandable text and multiple strings, is written as hex bytes. Each carries its type number as hex(n), except plain binary, which is written as hex. Lines wrap before column 78 with a trailing backslash. (PolicyPlus/RegFile.vb:117)

A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker, or when a delete-values list for the key names it, regardless of case. Entries are examined in sorted order, and a value whose name sorts after the marker is stored as present and cancels the deletion, whenever it was written and whichever marker kind came before. (PolicyPlus/PolicySource.vb:118)
Keys marked for removal are written to a REG file with a leading minus sign and values marked for deletion as a bare minus sign. (PolicyPlus/RegFile.vb:121)
